# Aunt Euphemia

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- **Role:** housemother  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Phemie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty  <sub>[v3 c25 P3](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0003), [v3 c35 P2](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Euphemia is a small, elderly woman with a gently triangular face and big, tender blue eyes brimming with youthfulness and expectation. She has rose-colored cheeks and silver-white hair styled in small rolls above her ears.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)_

## Personality

Aunt Euphemia is a happy, good-humoured housemother who lives by a philosophy of fulfilling her duties to God, others, and herself while enjoying life. Although she can speak sternly on matters of propriety, she faces circumstances with captivating elegance. She is readily won over by constant, respectful manners and possesses a lively sense of humour, though she considers Cressida Lindsay completely insane.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c20 P9](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0009), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)_

## History

Aunt Euphemia raised her daughter, Elizabeth, teaching her cooking before letting her pursue university studies and eventually depart for foreign mission work in India. Left alone in a large house, Aunt Euphemia agreed to move to Portmaris to manage Tabby's Place as a housemother for Nell Harcourt, Honora Hollis, and their companions. She arrived at Tabby's Place bringing along her gray-and-white cat, the Sarah-cat, and quickly endeared herself to the household. Over three winters, she served as a caring and beloved maternal figure to the girls living at the home, keeping the hearth warm, keeping company with the house cats, and welcoming their visiting friends.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c18 P2](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0002), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c37 P12](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0012)_

## Background by volume

- Named Jamesina after her father James who drowned a month before her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Grew up in a family with around six girls  <sub>[v3 c19 P42](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0042)</sub>
- Was forbidden by her mother and husband from having a yellow silk dress  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- Used to laugh at and mock her past suitors  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
- Advised a suitor to wear an elastic skull strip to flatten his ears  <sub>[v3 c37 P40](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0040)</sub>
- Received her gray-and-white cat, the Sarah-cat, as a gift from her laundress  <sub>[v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058)</sub>
- Taught her daughter cooking before allowing her to attend university  <sub>[v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006)</sub>

## Quotes

> Fulfill what you owe to God, to those around you, and to yourself, while enjoying your life. Such is the doctrine I live by, and it has served me quite effectively.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> Obtaining a yellow silk dress is the absolute first action I intend to take upon arriving in heaven.  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

> Deriding your suitors lacks propriety; however, it was my own constant habit.  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
